learning_outcomes.text: Have developed and integrated basic knowledge of metallic materials suitable for component fabrication using foundry and additive manufacturing technologies. Have gained awareness of issues related to physical metallurgy, relationships between microstructure and mechanical properties of ferrous and non-ferrous alloys. Be able to select appropriate materials and heat treatments for engineering design.
Apply the knowledge gained in a design context through lessons and in-class exercises.

Critically understand the characteristics and behavior of matter by evaluating its properties and suitability in relation to the intended applications. Process relevant data to verify required performance.
Have acquired sufficient language skills regarding the specific technological terminology of the teachings.

syllabus_topics: Brief introduction to crystallography
Diffusion phenomena correlated to the main heat treatments: I° and II° Fick’s law
Defects within the metallic materials
Phase diagrams: basic characteristics, lever rule, cooling pathways at the thermodynamic equilibrium
Phase diagram of Fe-Fe3C and microstructures
Strengthening mechanisms of the metallic materials
Solidification in conventional and innovative processes
Mechanical characterisation: Tensile test, hardness test, and Charpy impact test
Innovative production process: Metal additive manufacturing: general description, applications and operation of the machine
Process parameters
Advantages and Disadvantages of Metal additive manufacturing
Steel: Designation
The main microstructures obtained during the main industrial heat treatments
Heat treatments: quenching, annealing, tempering, normalizing
Nitriding and carburizing
Brief description of structural steels, special structural steels, tool steels, and stainless steels
Aluminium alloys: Designations
Main aluminium alloys: microstructure, mechanical properties and applications
Production of aluminium
Main heat treatments and effects induced by cold deformation
Additive Manufacturing of Aluminium alloys
Analysis of application cases and selection criteria for metallic materials
assessment_rules: The written exam is structured by 4 open questions and lasts 2 hours. The exam is passed if the total score is equal to or higher than 18/33. A score of "30 cum laude" is given if the total score is higher than 30/33 and precise vocabulary is used. Students may choose to take an oral exam to improve or worsen the written exam grade, provided the written score is 18/33 or higher. If a student scores 16/33 on the written exam, they may still pass by taking an oral exam.
